title: Additive rules self-emulate; rules 90 and 150 are the only elementary ones

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Additive rules self-emulate; rules 90 and 150 are the only elementary ones

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Every additive cellular automaton rule can emulate itself and therefore yields nested patterns, and among two-color nearest-neighbor rules the only fundamentally different additive rules are rules 90 and 150; self-emulation is otherwise rare, though non-additive examples such as rule 184 exist.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: one can show that any rule that is additive will be able to emulate itself and will thus yield nested patterns. But there are rather few additive rules, and indeed with two colors and nearest neighbors the only fundamentally different ones are precisely rules 90 and 150.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 6, “Starting from Randomness”; section “Special Initial Conditions” (from p. 266), p. 271. Scope: additive cellular automata, especially elementary rules

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch06-20: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.93

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Additivity is a finite algebraic property and the elementary-rule universe is exhaustively enumerable. The self-emulation implication can be checked symbolically, making the stated result reproducible now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Prove the block-rescaling identity for linear cellular automata over GF(2), enumerate all 256 elementary rules for additivity up to reflection and complementation, and verify the claimed non-additive rule 184 self-emulation. Any additional inequivalent additive rule refutes the enumeration.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
“Fundamentally different” requires explicit symmetry equivalences.

The precise self-emulation scale must be specified.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Additivity implies a binomial self-similarity identity, which is a proof that every additive rule emulates itself and produces nested patterns. Among the 256 elementary rules the linear ones can be listed exhaustively, and the claim that rules 90 and 150 are the only distinct cases is a finite check under stated symmetries. Rule 184's three-cell emulation is another finite identity. The word rare is the only soft residue.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test all 256 elementary rules for linearity over GF(2), reduce the linear ones by color swap and reflection, and check the claimed block emulations for rules 90, 150, and 184. An extra linear equivalence class, or a failed emulation identity, would refute the corresponding clause.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Rare, outside the elementary linear list, is a sample remark attached to a sharp classification.

Fundamentally different means up to the usual color and reflection symmetries.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: Among the 256 elementary cellular automata, every rule that is additive (linear over GF(2)) can emulate itself with blocks of cells and yields an exactly self-similar (nested) pattern from a single black cell; after removing trivial rules and identifying rules related by reflection or by the sublattice (shear) relation between rules 60 and 90, exactly two additive classes remain, represented by rules 90 and 150; self-emulation among the remaining 248 rules is uncommon, but rule 184 has it with blocks of three cells.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py tests all 256 elementary rules for GF(2)-linearity over all 64 neighbourhood pairs, then searches exhaustively for block self-emulations with b = 2, 3, 4 cells per block, t = 1..4 steps and all ordered pairs of distinct blocks, checking every arrangement of 2k+1 blocks (k = ceil(t/b)) so that the centre block's light cone is covered. Nesting of the non-trivial additive rules was checked as exact scale-2 self-similarity p[2t, 2i] = p[t, i] of the single-black-cell pattern over 256 steps, and the sublattice relation p90[t, 2j - t] = p60[t, j] was verified over 256 steps before being used to merge rules 60/102 with 90. Equivalence classes of non-trivial additive rules were formed by union-find under reflection and the verified sublattice relation.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Definitions: a rule f is additive iff f(x XOR y) = f(x) XOR f(y) for all pairs of 3-cell neighbourhoods x, y (which forces f(000) = 0). Rule f self-emulates with block size b >= 2 and t >= 1 steps iff there are two distinct b-cell blocks B0, B1 such that for every arrangement of 2k+1 blocks (k = ceil(t/b)) drawn from {B0, B1}, running f for t steps leaves the centre block equal to B_{f(c-1, c0, c1)}, where c-1, c0, c1 are the bits represented by the three central blocks; this is the block-emulation notion of NKS pp. 269-271 and note p. 1118, which allows t != b. The search covers b in {2, 3, 4}, t in {1, 2, 3, 4} and all block pairs. Trivial rules: 0, 204 (identity), 170 and 240 (shifts). Equivalences for 'fundamentally different': reflection (rule 60 <-> 102) and the sublattice relation p90[t, 2j - t] = p60[t, j], verified computationally on the first 256 steps from a single black cell. Nested: the single-cell pattern p satisfies p[2t, 2i] = p[t, i] for all 0 <= t < 256 and |i| <= t. Clause A passes if every additive rule self-emulates with b = t = 2 and every non-trivial additive rule is nested in this sense. Clause B passes if the non-trivial additive rules fall into exactly two equivalence classes, one containing 90 and one containing 150. Clause C passes if rule 184 self-emulates with b = 3 for some t <= 4 and the fraction of the 248 non-additive rules with at least one self-emulation in the searched range is <= 0.25. 'supports' if A, B and C all pass.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. 'refutes' if clause A or clause B fails (an additive rule that does not self-emulate with b = t = 2, a non-trivial additive rule that is not nested, or a third inequivalent non-trivial additive class). 'mixed' if A and B pass but C fails (rule 184 does not self-emulate with 3-cell blocks within the search, or self-emulation is found in more than 25 % of non-additive rules, so 'rather rare' would be an overstatement).

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: rule numbers; fraction of the 248 non-additive rules with at least one block self-emulation (b <= 4, t <= 4)

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: exhaustive finite check; exact within the searched block sizes and step counts

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: 'Additive' is read as linear over GF(2) (Wolfram's own definition on p. 264: patterns from two initial conditions can be superimposed by XOR). 'Emulate itself' is read as block emulation with 2 to 4 cells per block and 1 to 4 steps per emulated step. 'Fundamentally different' is read as 'not related by left-right reflection and not related by the sublattice/shear relation that maps the rule 60 pattern onto the even sublattice of the rule 90 pattern'; without the second identification rule 60 (and its mirror 102) would be a third additive rule, which the test records explicitly. 'Rather rare' is given the threshold 25 % of the non-additive rules. All patterns are generated by analysis.py; there is no external download.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: All 256 elementary cellular automata (Wolfram rule numbering), generated by analysis.py: additivity tables, exhaustive block self-emulation search (b = 2..4 cells, t = 1..4 steps, all block pairs), and 256-step single-black-cell patterns for the self-similarity and sublattice checks

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
All three pre-registered clauses passed: exactly 8 additive rules exist, each self-emulates with 2-cell blocks and 2 steps (the Frobenius identity f^2 = f at stride 2 over GF(2)) and the four non-trivial ones are exactly self-similar at scale 2; after identifying 60/102 with 90 through the verified sublattice relation the additive rules fall into the two classes {60, 90, 102} and {150}; rule 184 self-emulates with the 3-cell blocks 010/101 and 3 steps, as Wolfram says, and only 15 of the 248 non-additive rules (6 %) have any block self-emulation in the searched range.

'Fundamentally different' required an interpretive choice: rule 60 (and its mirror 102) is additive and nested but is not related to 90 by reflection or colour complement; it is the rule 90 pattern restricted to the sublattice i + t even. Without that identification the claim's 'precisely rules 90 and 150' would be 'rules 60, 90 and 150'. The test records this explicitly.

The 15 non-additive self-emulating rules are the affine rules 15, 51, 85, 153, 165, 195 (complements/XOR with 1), the AND/OR-type class-1 rules 128, 136, 192, 238, 252, 254, 255, the shift-like rule 226 and rule 184. Larger blocks or more steps (b > 4, t > 4) might reveal further self-emulating rules; 'rather rare' is confirmed only within the searched range.

The claim's sub-clause that additivity implies self-emulation in general (for any number of colours and neighbours) was tested only for the elementary rules; the argument via the Frobenius endomorphism is standard but was not checked beyond them.
